citation.title: Validation of Toroidal Rotation and Ion Temperature in KSTAR Plasmas
citation.authors: S. G. Lee; H. H. Lee; W. H. Ko; J. W. Yoo; KSTAR Team

topic: Comparison of core impurity toroidal rotation and ion temperature from XICS (Ar) and CES (C VI) in KSTAR. The paper also covers background-subtraction practice for CES.
own_question: Do simultaneous XICS and CES core rotation and Ti measurements from different impurity species agree across KSTAR discharges?
actual_method_and_evidence:
The paper is descriptive and qualitative. It shows time traces for ELMy and ELM-free H-modes, an ohmic beam-blip shot, ECRH rotation profiles and a long-pulse H-mode. Agreement is described as reasonable, with no quantitative error metrics.

CES uses the active C VI 529.05 nm line. It relies on NBI modulation for background subtraction, or on two-Gaussian fitting when there is no modulation. The stated CES time resolution is up to 10 ms. The paper attributes CES oscillations to low core signal-to-noise and possibly to mechanical vibration. Comparisons are core-only and do not use common flux surfaces. The XICS profiles are line-averaged and not inverted.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In KSTAR, reported carbon-impurity CES Ti depends on analysis choices: NBI-modulation background subtraction, or two-Gaussian active/background fitting when beams are unmodulated.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.3 Sec. II; p.5 Sec. III (Fig. 6 discussion)
claim_checks.qualification: The authors state that two-Gaussian results agree with modulation results when the active signal dominates or the Doppler shifts differ substantially. This is not quantified. It supports treating CES reports as conventional labels.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: KSTAR CES impurity Ti can show noise-driven fluctuations, and the paper reports time resolution up to 10 ms.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.3 Sec. II and Sec. III (Figs. 2-3 discussion)
claim_checks.qualification: The source makes this point for core channels, which are not the pedestal top. It covers an earlier campaign, not KSTAR2022. The vibration cause is speculative.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Up to 10 ms CES resolution is stated. Report latency and arrival times are not given.
validation_if_relevant: Qualitative cross-diagnostic agreement only. There is no independent truth, no statistics, and no data split.
forbidden_inferences: CES Ti is validated physical truth or main-ion Ti
The results apply to the pedestal-top chord or the 2022 campaign
The paper gives quantified XICS-CES agreement
The CES pipeline runs in real time
The paper involves BES/ECEI or nowcasting
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include as background on the provenance and processing of KSTAR CES impurity Ti labels and their noise. It also provides cross-diagnostic context. Cite it narrowly.
